title: Trumbauer remembers the boy in short pants
summary: Trumbauer passes Lester Young to greet Tate and praises his subtones.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: So there were a lot of people running to the steps wanting autographs and things and things -- you know, the band was shoutin' down and everybody was so -- the band was so popular and Lester was actually -- I didn't have near the solos that he had to play and he was the big thing, you know, he was already big, you know, name and everything, featured. So Frankie let him pass. I thought sure he was going to grab Lester, you know what I mean? And man, when I came off, he walked straight up to me and this knocked me out, man. You don't know how I felt, man. He let Pres. pass and Pres. had played like 15 more solos than I had -- he listened to him -- and that's who he loved.

Then -- and he came up to me and he says, -- I says, 'Aren't you --' He says -- I says, 'Aren't you Frankie Trumbauer?' He says, 'Yeah.' I says, 'I know it.' I says, 'I met you --' He cut me off to let me know he remembered me. I says, 'I met you --' He says, 'With Paul Whiteman,' he said, 'in Dallas.' He said, 'You had on short pants.' So you know what he said to me? I swear to God. He

says, "I see you practiced, you have practiced." He remembered he had -- I says, "You remember you told me that?" He says, "Sure, I remember." He says, "I see you practiced." He says, "You have the prettiest subtones of anybody I've ever heard in my life," I swear to God he told me that. He says, "Because you make them. When you go down to that B natural and B flat, you don't blast them." He say, "You subtoning and it sounds just like you're playing all over your horn." He says, "Keep that in." He said -- I swear to God. And we became friends after that, you know. I says, "Well, Lester Young, I got to bring him here to meet you," I said, "because he loves you." So he says, "He plays good." Then we went on, you know, and talked and talked and everytime I'd go to Kansas City, he was here. I says, "Well, what are you doing here?" He says, "I'm in aeronautics." You running out?
